references.text: Isaac prepares a meal for Abimelech and his company after making a covenant, which mirrors Jacob's actions with Laban.
Jacob and Laban make a covenant, and the men gather stones and eat together, leading up to the sacrifice and meal in verse 54.
Jacob offers sacrifices to God at Beersheba before going to Egypt, showing Jacob's consistent practice of offering to God at key moments.
Jethro offers sacrifices to God, and Aaron and the elders of Israel come to eat bread with him before God—a close parallel to Jacob's sacrifice and shared meal on the mountain.
Moses sends young men to offer sacrifices, and then the elders of Israel eat and drink before God on the mountain, mirroring Jacob's sacrifice and meal on the mountain.
David buys the threshing floor of Araunah to build an altar and offer sacrifices to the Lord, an act of offering at a specific place to honor God.
Direct continuation of the same event: The covenant feast at the stone heap (v.46) culminates in the sacrificial meal on the mountain (v.54).
A clear theological contrast between a holy covenant meal (Jacob) and a sinful act involving eating blood (the people).
Thematic parallel: Offering as thanksgiving and response to God's intervention (peace between relatives versus deliverance from a storm).
